= The IETF incident fixture

This directory is the executable form of the originating acceptance case in
https://github.com/hyperpolymath/empty-linter/issues/74[issue #74].

== The incident

An Internet-Draft was repeatedly rejected by the IETF Datatracker because an
editor had inserted a hidden formatting character into the submitted text.
The fault was invisible, so the rejection was unactionable. `empty-linter`
exists to make that class of fault visible, locatable, safely repairable,
and verifiably gone.

== What is planted

`build-fixture.js` deterministically writes `draft-rfc-style.txt` with exactly
three plantings (all written as explicit numeric code points, reviewable in
a plain diff):

[cols="1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
| Planting | Where | Expected handling

| U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE
| abstract, between "network" and "layer" — the incident character
| detected as *mechanical*; proposed as replace-with-space; applied produces
an inspectable patch with no unrelated changes

| U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER
| inside the word "dataformats"
| detected as *semantic*; the repair policy must refuse to touch it, and it
must survive repair byte-for-byte

| Zalgo run (5 combining marks on one base)
| the "artist's impression" line
| detected by the suspicious-combining-run detector; preserved by the default
policy after review
|===

The remaining text (RFC-style header block, ruler, section headings) is the
negative control: nothing else in the file may produce a finding.

== What the E2E test asserts

`tests/IetfIncident_test.js` walks the whole product over this file and pins,
for issue #74's fixture bullets:

* exact code point *and* UTF-8 bytes in the report;
* file, line, Unicode-scalar column (not a UTF-16 index), byte offset;
* visible escaped context plus the character name, official Unicode name, and
  general category;
* safety classification — mechanical / semantic / ambiguous — per planting;
* an inspectable patch whose application changes only the accepted finding;
* SHA-256 input/output hashes, a provenance record, and a *successful rescan*
  record proving the accepted class of fault is gone while the semantic and
  reviewed plantings still stand;
* audit mode never mutating the input.

The test also asserts the checked-in `draft-rfc-style.txt` is byte-identical
to `build-fixture.js`'s output, so the fixture can never silently drift from
its generator.

== Regenerating

[source,bash]
----
bun run tests/fixtures/ietf-incident/build-fixture.js
bun test tests/IetfIncident_test.js   # must pass, byte-identical
----
